title: GMRES: Add Kokkos kernels for orthogonalization with device vectors

commits.author: Martin Kronbichler
commits.subject: GMRES: Add Kokkos kernels for orthogonalization with device vectors
commits.body:
For LinearAlgebra::distributed::Vector<Number, MemorySpace::Default>,
SolverGMRES and SolverFGMRES previously fell back to the generic
implementation, which computes one inner product (with its own device
synchronization and MPI reduction) per basis vector and updates the new
vector once per basis vector.

Add Kokkos implementations of the three kernels used by classical
Gram-Schmidt and delayed classical Gram-Schmidt:
- do_Tvmult_add: all inner products in one sweep, using a team
  policy with register blocking over 8 basis vectors and a deterministic
  second-stage reduction, followed by a single transfer to the host,
- do_subtract_and_norm: fused vector update and norm,
- do_add: fused linear combination for the solution update.

The persistent device data lives in a new OrthogonalizationData struct.

title: FEEvaluation: reuse the separate-vector/FESystem distinction in read_write_operation

commits.author: Mohit Prajapati
commits.subject: FEEvaluation: reuse the separate-vector/FESystem distinction in read_write_operation
commits.body:
read_write_operation() re-derives the same condition
(n_components == 1 || this->n_fe_components == 1) at four places to tell
whether the n_components copies of a vector-valued quantity live in
separate vectors or interleaved in one FESystem-based vector. Compute it
once as separate_vectors and reuse it, matching what 49bfb1fc5b did for
read_write_operation_contiguous().

The branches themselves are left alone. Two of them differ in loop
nesting order rather than only in indexing, so merging them would change
the order in which the gather and scatter loops walk memory. I also tried
folding the src_ptrs setup into a single loop over a computed bound, but
that replaces two compile-time trip counts with a runtime one and costs
gcc about 2.8% more instructions in this function, so it is left as an
if/else too.

No functional change intended. Addresses more of #16006.

commits.subject: Fix CylindricalManifold::push_forward_gradient() angle derivative
commits.body:
push_forward() scales the rotated direction by the radius r, so
d/dphi of the mapped point is r*(-sin(phi)*n + cos(phi)*(d x n)).
The angle column of the gradient was missing the factor r, which
made the Jacobian wrong for every r != 1 (e.g. MappingManifold on
cylindrical geometries).

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: DataOutInterface::write_vtu_in_parallel(): simplify implementation
commits.body:
Let every rank assemble a contiguous chunk of the final file, with rank 0
prepending the header and the last rank appending the footer. This way a
single MPI_Exscan and a single collective write suffice, and we no longer
need to broadcast the header size and write header and footer separately.

Also avoid repeated (and expensive) copies of the stringstream buffer and
drop the unused MPI_Info object.

SparsityPattern: avoid quadratic complexity in Cuthill McKee algorithm

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: SparsityTools::reorder_Cuthill_McKee(): fix quadratic complexity
commits.body:
For every new connected component of the graph the function scanned all
rows twice: once to check for unnumbered indices, and once to find a new
starting index with minimal coordination number. This leads to O(C * N)
complexity for C components, which is quadratic for a block-diagonal
sparsity pattern (e.g., dG without flux couplings).

Count numbered indices instead. Once a second component is encountered,
sort all rows by coordination number and advance an index through this
list for finding new starting indices. The resulting numbering is
unchanged.

Timings (hyper_cube in 2D, refined r times, release mode):

                  r     n_dofs        old        new
    FE_DGQ(1)     5       4096    0.0056s   0.00022s
                  6      16384     0.090s   0.00065s
                  7      65536      1.35s    0.0026s
                  8     262144      21.4s     0.011s
                  9    1048576          -     0.045s
                 10    4194304          -      0.18s
    FE_Q(1)       8      66049    0.0038s    0.0043s
                 10    1050625     0.066s     0.070s
                 12   16785409      1.23s      1.28s

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: parallel::TriangulationBase: fix stale ghost vertices in communicate_locally_moved_vertices()
commits.body:
A vertex is owned by the lowest subdomain id of its adjacent cells. A ghost
cell can therefore contain a vertex whose owner has no cell that is a ghost
on the receiving process. communicate_locally_moved_vertices() only sent
moved vertices from their owner, so such ghost cells kept stale positions.

Fix this by a second exchange that sends all vertices of locally owned
cells, which are up to date after the first exchange.

title: Implement gradient transforms in MappingFEField

commits.author: Malo Le Scoul
commits.subject: As requested, I added a test to verify the MappingFEField gradient transform implementations by comparing them with MappingQ for a translated FE field in 2D and 3D. Using a nontrivial affine geometry, and therefore a non-identity Jacobian, exposed an ordering error in my implementation of mapping_contravariant_gradient, where the covariant and contravariant factors were swapped; this has now been corrected. The test also uses nonsymmetric input tensors to make index and transpose errors detectable. In addition, dynamic_cast is now only used in a debug assertion to verify the InternalData type, while static_cast is used for the actual access, following the usual deal.II pattern.

title: Add codimension-one support to FE_RaviartThomasNodal

commits.author: Jakob Tore Kammeyer Nielsen
commits.subject: Added missing blank line to expected test output

commits.author: Jakob Tore Kammeyer Nielsen
commits.subject: Add codimension-one support to FE_RaviartThomasNodal
commits.body:
Template FE_RaviartThomasNodal on both dim and spacedim and instantiate it
for the codimension-one case dim=2, spacedim=3. On a surface mesh the element
represents a spacedim-valued vector field that is everywhere tangential to the
surface, obtained from the reference-cell Raviart-Thomas shape functions via
the surface Piola transform u = J u_hat / sqrt(det(J^T J)). The element has
n_components == spacedim so that the field can be accessed as a spacedim-valued
vector through FEValuesExtractors::Vector.

The hanging-node / hp interface constraints (computed via
FETools::compute_face_embedding_matrices) are only available for dim==spacedim
and are guarded with `if constexpr`; the codimension-one element can be used on
surface meshes without hanging nodes.

Document the surface use case, including the non-conforming behaviour on
non-C^1 manifolds and the currently unimplemented features for the
codimension-one case.

Add a test that verifies the element is tangential to a tilted surface mesh
and reports spacedim components, and a second test that checks the shape
values at quadrature points processed by the scalar remainder path of
MappingQ, guarding the volume_elements fix in the previous commit.

commits.author: Jakob Tore Kammeyer Nielsen
commits.subject: Support codimension-one case in FE_PolyTensor
commits.body:
FE_PolyTensor stores reference-cell shape gradients and Hessians as
DerivativeForm<1/2, dim, spacedim> objects. The assignment of the
polynomial-space gradients (Tensor<2, dim>) and Hessians (Tensor<3, dim>)
into these objects, both in get_data() and in compute_fill(), relied on a
DerivativeForm/Tensor conversion that asserts dim == spacedim.

Guard each such assignment with `if constexpr (dim == spacedim)` and fall
back to a row-by-row copy for the codimension-one case (dim < spacedim),
where only the first `dim` rows are populated. The storage type is kept as
DerivativeForm (rather than Tensor) so that the mapping_none / covariant
gradient paths, which call Mapping::transform() on the DerivativeForm
overload, keep working for elements such as FE_BernardiRaugel.

Add an explicit instantiation of FE_PolyTensor<2, 3>. This is a
prerequisite for Raviart-Thomas elements on embedded surfaces.

commits.author: Jakob Tore Kammeyer Nielsen
commits.subject: Fix FEValuesViews::Vector for non-primitive elements on codim-1 meshes
commits.body:
In the non-primitive branch (single_nonzero_component == -1), the value,
gradient, divergence, Hessian, third-derivative and symmetric-gradient
accessors of FEValuesViews::Vector looped over only the first `dim`
components of the return value. On a codimension-one mesh (dim < spacedim)
this dropped the out-of-plane components (e.g. the z-component for
dim=2, spacedim=3) of a non-primitive vector-valued shape function.

Loop over `spacedim` components instead; the backing
is_nonzero_shape_function_component[] array is already sized spacedim, so
this is a no-op for the dim == spacedim case and fixes the codim-1 case.

title: FEEvaluation: consolidate separate-vector/FESystem branches in read_write_operation_contiguous

commits.author: Mohit Prajapati
commits.subject: FEEvaluation: consolidate separate-vector/FESystem branches in read_write_operation_contiguous
commits.body:
The contiguous-storage path in read_write_operation_contiguous() repeatedly
re-derives whether a vector-valued quantity is stored as n_components
separate vectors or interleaved in a single FESystem-based vector, using
the same condition (n_components == 1 || this->n_fe_components == 1) at
each of several call sites. Compute this once as separate_vectors and
reuse it, and fold the resulting near-identical loop bodies together where
they differ only by index offset or vector selection.

No functional change intended. Addresses one instance of the duplicated
component-handling pattern described in #16006; the same pattern recurs
elsewhere in this file and is left for follow-up patches.

title: ReferenceCell::new_isotropic_*: use references.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: ReferenceCell::new_isotropic_*: use references.
commits.body:
Previously we copied these tables every time we needed them. That took
up a small but measurable amount of runtime (about 2.5% of
execute_refinement_isotropic()). It is much more efficient to set up the
tables once and return references.

Since (in C++17, this is fixed in C++20) constexpr functions cannot
contain static constexpr members we have to remove constexpr from these
functions. This doesn't have any impact (the generated code is the same
- i.e., execute_refinement_isotropic() executes exactly the same number
of instructions).

title: base/*polynomials_base.h: fix compilation with Clang and Cuda with C++20

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: base/*polynomials_base.h: fix compilation with Clang and Cuda with C++20
commits.body:
This is a subtle one:

A destructor defaulted on its *first* declaration is treated like an *implicit* destructor and in the case of both `*PolynomialsBase` classes inferred to be `__host__ __device__`. That inference would propagate to the implicit destructors of all derived classes and fail "device" compilation, because `Polynomials::Polynomial`'s destructor is a host-only function.

A destructor defaulted outside the class is user-provided and remains a host function (when not annotated).

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove macOS-specific -rdynamic and -ftemplate-depth handling
commits.body:
The -rdynamic strip carried a long-standing "check whether this is
still necessary" TODO. It is not: the flag is only ever added by
enable_if_links(), which test-links with -Werror first, so a toolchain
that rejects or warns about -rdynamic never receives it and there is
nothing to strip.

The -ftemplate-depth=1024 flag raised an allegedly too-low default
template instantiation depth of old AppleClang versions. Clang has
long defaulted to a depth of 1024 -- the C++ standard's recommended
minimum (Annex B) and exactly the value set here -- as verified by
clang's own test suite [1], so the flag is redundant on all supported
AppleClang versions (12+).

[1] clang/test/SemaTemplate/instantiation-depth-default.cpp

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove -fuse-ld=gold workaround for expand_instantiations
commits.body:
This worked around a hang when linking expand_instantiations with
ld.gold and -pthread, see https://github.com/dealii/dealii/issues/1798
(2015). The build system has not added -fuse-ld=gold itself for years
-- it only auto-selects mold or lld -- so the filter could only ever
trigger for users passing the flag manually. The gold linker itself is
on its way out: it is deprecated as of binutils 2.44, whose main
release tarball no longer even contains the gold sources [1].

[1] https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/info-gnu/2025-02/msg00001.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove configure test for C++14 relaxed constexpr support
commits.body:
The test probed whether the compiler correctly allows calling
non-constexpr functions from constexpr functions in unevaluated
branches, as specified by C++14 (N3652). GCC >= 5 and Clang >= 3.4
implement C++14 constexpr correctly [1], far below our minimum
supported versions (GCC 9, Clang 10). MSVC remains special-cased:
it is known to crash with an internal compiler error on our
constexpr code even when a simple test passes (see #9080), so
DEAL_II_CXX14_CONSTEXPR_BUG stays unconditionally set there, as
before.

[1] https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/compiler_support/14

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: use git --date=iso-strict unconditionally
commits.body:
The --date=iso-strict option was introduced in git 2.2, released in
November 2014 [1]. Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, the oldest platform we care
about, ships git 2.25, so the version check and fallback are no
longer needed.

[1] https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/Documentation/RelNotes/2.2.0.adoc

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: simplify OpenMP SIMD flag selection for Intel compilers
commits.body:
Intel deprecated -openmp in favor of -qopenmp with the 15.0 release
(2014) and removed the old spelling in later releases (release 18
no longer accepts it). Compilers older than icc 15 cannot build our
C++17 code base anyway (we already warn about icc < 19), and both
icc >= 15 and the IntelLLVM-based icpx accept -qopenmp, so the
version check is unnecessary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: set DEAL_II_FALLTHROUGH unconditionally to [[fallthrough]]
commits.body:
[[fallthrough]] is a core language attribute of C++17 (P0188R1), which
deal.II requires unconditionally: configuration aborts if the C++17
feature test fails. All supported compilers implement it (GCC 7+,
Clang 3.9+, MSVC 19.10+ [1]), well below our respective minimum
versions. This makes the two configure-time compile checks for
[[fallthrough]] and the __attribute__((fallthrough)) fallback
unnecessary.

[1] https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/compiler_support/17

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove check for libc++ std::bind bug (LLVM #20084)
commits.body:
Old libc++ versions could not invoke the result of std::bind to a
const member function, see
  https://llvm.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=20084
The bug was fixed in libc++ in 2014. Any libc++ shipped alongside our
minimum supported compilers (Clang 10 / AppleClang 12, both from 2020)
contains the fix, so the check can no longer fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove check for clang <= 3.5 auto return type bug
commits.body:
Clang up to version 3.5 emitted a spurious error for an undeduced auto
return type when compiling with debug information, see
  https://llvm.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=16876
The bug was fixed in the clang 3.6 release cycle (2014). We require
Clang 10 (and AppleClang 12), so the check can no longer fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove string(REPEAT) fallback for CMake < 3.15
commits.body:
The string(REPEAT) subcommand was introduced in CMake 3.15 [1]. We now
require CMake 3.16, so the manual character-by-character padding loop
for older versions is dead code.

[1] https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/release/3.15.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: raise minimum required CMake version to 3.16
commits.body:
Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, the oldest platform we care about, ships CMake 3.16.3
[1]; every other supported distribution and macOS/Homebrew provide
newer versions. Raising the minimum from 3.13.4 to 3.16 allows us to
remove fallback code paths for older CMake versions from the build
system.

[1] https://packages.ubuntu.com/focal/cmake

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove -Wno-long-double flag check on macOS
commits.body:
-Wno-long-double was a flag of the Apple-modified GCC in the GCC 3.x/4.x
era and does not exist in any compiler we support (GCC 9+, Clang 10+,
AppleClang 12+) -- the comment itself already noted that newer compilers
dropped it. The enable_if_supported() call is therefore a guaranteed
no-op.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove Cygwin exclusion for compressed debug sections
commits.body:
The exclusion goes back to a mailing list report from February 2012.
Cygwin (and MinGW) with GNU compilers has been rejected with a fatal
error in check_02_system_features.cmake since 2015 (first released in
deal.II 8.4), and the flags are only added via enable_if_supported()/
enable_if_links(), i.e. after an actual compile/link test, so a
platform that cannot handle them never receives them anyway.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove blacklist for icc 16.0.1
commits.body:
Intel 16.0.1 (released 2015) miscompiled tests/fe/curl_curl_01.debug,
see https://github.com/dealii/dealii/issues/2203. deal.II now requires
C++17, which icc only reached (partially) with version 19, so version
16.0.1 cannot build the library in the first place and the blacklist
is dead code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove -no-vec workaround for icc < 15.0.3
commits.body:
This disabled vectorization to avoid miscompilation with Intel 13.1/14,
see https://code.google.com/p/dealii/issues/detail?id=156. deal.II now
requires C++17, which these compilers do not support: we already warn
about icc older than 19 in setup_compiler_flags_intel.cmake, and icc
only reached (partial) C++17 with version 19 [1]. The version branch
can no longer be taken by any compiler able to build the library.

[1] https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/news/c17-features-supported-by-c-compiler.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove workaround for FindBLAS bug in CMake 3.11
commits.body:
CMake 3.11 leaked the imported target name "PkgConfig::PKGC_BLAS" into
BLAS_LIBRARIES when BLA_PREFER_PKGCONFIG was set, see
  https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/17934
This only ever affected CMake 3.11, which is older than our minimum
required version 3.13.4, so the filter is dead code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: remove obsolete if(POLICY CMP0025) guard
commits.body:
Policy CMP0025 (distinguishing AppleClang from Clang in
CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID) was introduced in CMake 3.0 [1]. Since we require
CMake 3.13.4 the policy always exists and the guard is always true, so
the AppleClang version check can be unconditional.

[1] https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0025.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: CMake: work around a `ctest --launch` bug that eats our stdin

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: work around a ctest --launch bug that eats our stdin
commits.body:
ctest --launch (with CTEST_USE_LAUNCHERS) fails to forward its own
stdin to the launched process on many CMake/CTest releases (3.28
through 4.1+, backported inconsistently). expand_instantiations then
reads an empty file and aborts with
"Invalid instantiation list: missing 'for'".

Instead, let's redirect via execute_process()'s INPUT_FILE/OUTPUT_FILE
and a small cmake wrapper file instead.

Bug: https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/27610

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: parallel::shared::Triangulation: synchronize flags in prepare_coarsening_and_refinement()

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: tests: add regression test for shared_tria flag synchronization
commits.body:
Add tests/sharedtria/refine_and_coarsen_03, which sets refinement and
coarsening flags on locally owned cells only and then calls
prepare_coarsening_and_refinement() directly, as is customary before
attaching data for a solution transfer. The test counts refine and
coarsen flags over all active cells (including artificial ones)
immediately after the call and asserts that the counts agree across
MPI processes. The mpirun=1 and mpirun=3 output files report
identical cell counts before and after refinement, confirming that
flag smoothing no longer depends on the partitioning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: parallel::shared::Triangulation: synchronize flags in prepare_coarsening_and_refinement()
commits.body:
Each MPI process only needs to set refinement and coarsening flags on its
own locally owned cells; so far the flags were only synchronized over all
processes in execute_coarsening_and_refinement(). If a user calls
prepare_coarsening_and_refinement() directly (as is customary before
attaching data for a solution transfer), flag smoothing thus ran with only
the locally owned flags visible. In particular, the rule that a group of
sibling cells is only coarsened if all children are flagged then deletes
coarsening flags of families straddling a partition boundary, and the
resulting mesh depends on the partitioning.

Factor the flag synchronization out of execute_coarsening_and_refinement()
into a helper function communicate_refinement_and_coarsening_flags() and
call it from a new prepare_coarsening_and_refinement() override as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: FEValuesBase: simplify and correct connections.
commits.body:

FEValuesBase gets a cell it sets up signals for refinement and

title: Improve error messages in FiniteElement::get_sub_fe().
DerivativeApproximation: use type erasure.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: DerivativeApproximation: use type erasure.
commits.body:
This prevents WorkStream::run() from seeing the type of the calling
function (which includes the vector type), which in turn prevents it
from instantiating a copy of itself for every vector type (and dim, and
spacedim, etc.) used by the calling function. In practice, this
dramatically lowers the size of the object file (89 MB to 24 MB).

Since the worker function sets up an hp::FEValues object, examines
neighboring cells, etc. converting this from a normal function call to a
virtual one is not a measurable amount of overhead (TaskFlow can't
inline the function call anyway since it is ultimately stored as
std::function<void()> in its task graph).

title: CellId: update the binary encoding to work with Pyramids.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: CellId: update the binary encoding to work with Pyramids.
commits.body:
While we are at it, also handle coarse cells larger than the largest
unsigned int.

Since a Pyramid can have 10 children, we need to support more than 2**3
children in 3d. To keep things simple, lets just use a 4-bit encoding of
each child index independent of the dimension. With 4 unsigned ints, we
should have 128 bytes available for child indices: that's enough for all
30 (via the 4-bit encoding, which is 120 bytes) plus one extra for the
number of child indices.

I also had to modify a test to not use as many refinement levels because
the lines (corresponding to a complete serialization) were too long for
numdiff.

commits.subject: EnableObserverPointer: let "" denote a missing object name.
commits.body:
Since the string "unknown subscriber" has 19 characters (with a NUL) it
is too long for the libstdc++ small-string limit of 16 (but not the
libc++ limit of 24). Hence, if we call subscribe() or unsubscribe() with
no object name (the common case!) we allocate that string (i.e., convert
it from a string literal to a std::string).

Since we use "unknown subscriber" for 100% of empty names, we can
instead let the empty name mean exactly that and move that string
literal into the exception itself to completely avoid the allocation.

title: Add our own implementation of std::inplace_vector.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: Add std_cxx26::inplace_vector.
commits.body:
std::inplace_vector is a dynamic version of std::array: it has a
built-in buffer and tracks the number of objects in that buffer. This
makes it ideal for small buffers who have a known maximum size (like the
number of vertices per cell) but unknown actual size.

There are a few things missing from this implementation:
1. Since we only require C++17 it does not support ranges.
2. Not everything which should be constexpr is constexpr. This part is
   tricky since C++ adds more constexpr functionality in each release,
   so some things (like constexpr delete) aren't possible in this class.

The primary advantage of having our own version of this class is that we
can add whatever subset of constexpr functionality we need: e.g., making
its constexpr functions work with fundamental types should be fine, but
isn't done yet. Another advantage is that the API is slightly different
than boost::static_vector.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: DynamicSparsityPattern: optimize and avoid allocations.
commits.body:
Rather than ad-hoc searching, we can just scan through everything once
and combine the new indices and existing ones with std::set_union().
Rather than more complex algorithms, just use std::lower_bound() for the
unsorted case. This is about 0-20% faster (measured by step-40, for
sorted indices, and step-69, for unsorted).

Furthermore, this lowers the number of allocations by about 25%.

commits.subject: CMake: Bugfix: add missing test dependency on ${_source_file}
commits.body:
The custom command that runs a test depends on ${_target}, which in case
of a "test.cc" variant is simply the test executable target. But for
"test.prm" variants the ${_target} is a specified executable and we
simply forgot to also depend on "test.prm" itself, aka the
${_source_file} in this case. Add this dependency so that tests are
rerun properly when the prm file changes.

taskflow is simply enabled by default. If we set the cached variable, on
the other hand, we *force* to have taskflow enabled. This is a problem
in scenarios where bundled libraries cannot be used...

benchmark, I was computing the covariant about 10 places per cell - its
easy enough to just compute it once and store it with the rest of the
transformation.

I elected to unconditionally compute the covariant (and determinant of
the contravariant in the last PR) since they are constant on each cell
and needed most of the time.

commits.author: Guilhem Poy
commits.subject: Fixing the compression bug of FETools::extrapolate.
commits.body:
Due to the different compress(insert) behaviour of Petsc/Trilinos and
LinearAlgebra::distributed vectors, the previous version of the
extrapolate method was failing with the latter type of vector on
distributed simulations with locally owned DoF at the interface between
a locally owned coarse cell and a more refined neighbouring ghost cell.

This bug was not detected before by the fe_tools_extrapolate_*** tests
of the testsuite because the tested triangulation included no such DoFs.
A simple mirror inversion of the refinement pattern allows to detect the
bug without having to change the tested outputs (the extrapolated
function is invariant under the inversion symmmetry), and was also
included in this commit in addition to the fix.

commits.author: Guilhem Poy
commits.subject: Modifies the testing of FETools::Extrapolate.
commits.body: This modification ensures that the compression failure of LinearAlgebra::distributed::Vector is properly detected by modifying the test triangulation with a simple inversion symmetry of the refinement pattern. It does not change the norms of solution vector evaluated during the testing since the tested function is invariant under the inversion symmetry. However, it introduces locally owned DoFs at interfaces between coarse locally owned cells and refined ghost cells, which is precisely the reason the compression failure arises.

incorrect when using nvcc leading to the compiler error
```
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/include/amxtileintrin.h(42): error:
identifier "__builtin_ia32_ldtilecfg" is undefined
    __builtin_ia32_ldtilecfg (__config);
```

Work around this by patching at least the bundled boost.

closes #17401

title: CMake: fix release/debug only configure with CMake 3.30

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: fix "Release" and "Debug" only configure for CMake 3.30
commits.body:
Beginning with version 3.30 CMake makes it an error to specify a
nonexistent target in a call to target_link_libraries() even if that
target is never used internally and only part of the exported interface.
This is a problem as we want to add configuration dependent targets with
a generator expression that are later exported:

  $<$<CONFIG:Release>:dealii::dealii_release> (...)

Note that we cannot simply use $<$<CONFIG:Release>:dealii_release> as
CMake then does not complete "dealii_release" to "dealii::dealii_release"
upon target export...

As a workaround we create alias targets with the "dealii::" namespace,
which makes the call to target_link_libraries() succeed.

title: Remove another duplicated table.
Explicitly use the inverse orientation instead of hard-coding.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: Explicitly use the inverse orientation instead of hard-coding.
commits.body:
Partially reverts #15678.

While #15678 fixed the permutation bug, it didn't address the true cause of the
problem: since face orientations are computed in the "apply this permutation to
face 1 to get face 2" direction, QProjector should use inverse orientations.
Since 2d orientations are their own inverses this only shows up in 3d.

Whenever two faces abutt, the first face is always in the default orientation
and the second face's orientation is computed relative to that (as decribed
here). Hence, when we project quadrature points onto the first face they do not
need to reoriented. However, we need to apply the *reverse* permutation on the
second face so that they end up in the same positions as the first face. More
formally: most, but not all, orientations are their own inverses. In particular,
triangle orientations 3 and 5 are each-other's inverses.

This matches the notion of inverse orientation used in #16828 for hypercubes. In
the future, we should combine the hypercube and non-hypercube implementations to
avoid these kinds of inconsistencies.

Part of #14667.

title: distributed/tria.cc: avoid FPE due to undefined behavior

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: distributed/tria.cc: avoid FPE due to undefined behavior
commits.body:
The following construct
```
static_cast<types::subdomain_id>(this_sc_point[dim])
```
triggers a floating point exception when the stored double is -1.0 (at
least with gcc-11 and avx512 instructions enabled).

Judging from cppreference [1] this is undefined behavior:
"""
A prvalue of floating-point type can be converted to a prvalue of any
integer type. The fractional part is truncated, that is, the fractional
part is discarded.

If the truncated value cannot fit into the destination type, the
behavior is undefined (even when the destination type is unsigned,
modulo arithmetic does not apply).
"""

Thus, work around the issue by explicitly setting negative values to
`numbers::invalid_subdomain_id` if we encounter -1.

[1] https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/implicit_conversion

title: Fix segmentation fault when using mpich

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: base/mpi.h: mark a template variable to have "const inline" linkage.

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: base/mpi.cc: remove superfluous explicit instantiations of template variable
commits.body:
The `mpi.h` header already contains:
```
template <typename T>
const MPI_Datatype mpi_type_id_for_type = /* implementation detail */;
```
Meaning, the variable is known fully after including the header.
Furthermore, the `const` qualifier marks the (template) variable as
`static`. I.e., it has internal linkage.

Thus, we must not explicitly instantiate the variables (suggesting
"extern" linkage in all but the `mpi.cc` compilation unit). This
apparently not an issue with OpenMPI because `MPI_Datatype` is a
complex data structure. But it is an issue with mpich where
`MPI_Datatype` is a simple `int` - leading to a segmentation fault when
during program startup.

title: Tensor<k, dim, Number::unroll(): fix copy statement

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: Tensor<k, dim, Number::unroll(): fix copy statement
commits.body:
The task for the rank-1 case is to copy all values from the internal
values array to the iterator range, so let us just use
```
  std::copy(std::begin(values), std::end(values), begin);
```
for this. The problem with the `&values[dim]` statement is the fact that
values[dim] is an out-of-bounds access and the address of if is
undefined.

```
../source/base/tensor.cc:52:5:   required from 'void dealii::{anonymous}::calculate_svd_in_place(dealii::Tensor<2, dim, Number>&, dealii::Tensor<2, dim, Number>&) [with int dim = 1; Number = float]'
../source/base/tensor.cc:85:25:   required from 'dealii::Tensor<2, dim, Number> dealii::project_onto_orthogonal_tensors(const dealii::Tensor<2, dim, Number>&) [with int dim = 1; Number = float]'
../source/base/tensor.cc:92:60:   required from here
../include/deal.II/base/tensor.h:1728:51: warning: parameter 'end' set but not used [-Wunused-but-set-parameter]
 1728 |                                    const Iterator end) const
      |
```

This is of course bogus, the compiler simply lost track of the
`if constexpr(...)` branch. This is fixed in later gcc versions. Let's
simply use the usual `(void)parameter` strategy to make gcc-9.4 happy.

title:
Classes used by Step 89 

The purpose of the classes is as follows:

PrecomputedFEEvaluationData stores the values and gradients for all requested points.
PrecomputedFEEvaluationDataView gives a structured access to the values/gradients of a cell/face via get_shift()
FERemoteEvaluationCommunicator fills the values/gradients in data using RPE
FERemoteEvaluation is a class similar to FEEvaluation but accessing precomputed/cached values/gradients in PrecomputedFEEvaluationData. The values/gradients of all points are updated via gather_evaluate(vector, flags). The function reinit() shifts the view to the current cell/face. The functions get_value() and get_gradient() give access to the value/gradient of the specified cell.

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: tests: add unit tests for dealii::Lazy<T>

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: base: Implement a Lazy<T> wrapper
commits.body:
Implement an optimized, thin wrapper that provides a convenient
mechanism for lazy initialization of the contained object on first use.
The class ensures that on-demand initialization of some expensive data
structure happens (a) in a thread-safe manner, and that (b) subsequent
checks in hot paths are cheap:

 - The class implements proper copy and move semantics inherited from
   std::optional. This is particularly desirable for our typical use
   case in deal.II where we want to initialize some payload exactly once
   (and simply copy or move it along with the container).

 - The "passive" call, i.e., when the object is already initialized is
   much cheaper than a call to std::call_once, or thread synchronization
   with a std::shared_mutex (because the initialize() or
   value_or_initialize() functions are inlined and consist of a mere
   check of a boolean followed by a conditional jump).

commits.body:
Most of the compilation work for FEValues is actually the inner functions used
by FEValuesViews objects. Explicitly instantiating these functions in their own
translation unit significantly lowers compilation time. Here are the numbers for
release mode:

master:
- fe_values_views: 7:58 wall time, 4.5 GB max RSS

feature:
- fe_values_views: 0:32 wall time, 1.6 GB max RSS
- fe_values_views_internal: 2:58 wall time, 2.8 GB max RSS

I had to adjust the type signatures (on the first ArrayView argument) to avoid
instantiating things for 'const float' rather than float et al.

title: Split fe_values.h and fe_values.cc into three files each.

commits.author: David Wells
commits.subject: Split fe_values.h and fe_values.cc into three files each.
commits.body:
In 367243a1614 (PR 15575) I removed SPLIT_INSTANTIATIONS_INDEX et al from
fe_values.cc. This was fine for -O2 but with -O3 -march=native this file now
takes several minutes to compile.

The majority of our compilation time here is in FEValuesViews - ultimately I'd
like to split that up. This commit performs one step towards splitting that up
by splitting up fe_values.h and corresponding source files into files for
FEValuesViews, FEValues, and FEValuesBase.

title: CMake: enable -ffp-exceptions-behavior=strict when compiling with clang

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: CMake: enable -ffp-exceptions-behavior=strict when compiling with clang
commits.body:
We have to ensure that we emit floating-point instructions in debug mode
that preserve the occurence of floating-point exceptions and don't
introduce new ones. gcc plays nicely in this regard by enabling
`-ftrapping-math` per default, at least for the level of optimization we
have in debug mode. clang however is more aggressive and assumes that it
can optimize code disregarding precise floating-point exception
semantics.

We thus set `-ffp-exceptions-behavior=strict` in debug mode to ensure
that our testsuite doesn't run into false positive floating-point
exceptions. See https://github.com/dealii/dealii/issues/15496

title: Test scalapack/*: restrict all scalapack tests to less than 10 mpi ranks

commits.author: Matthias Maier
commits.subject: Test scalapack/*: restrict all scalapack tests to less than 10 mpi ranks
commits.body:
Let us restrict the maximal concurrency of scalapack tests to less than
10 MPI ranks:

 - The purpose of these tests is to test our interfaces to scalapack and
   not whether scalapack functions properly for high(er) MPI
   concurrency. As such testing a few variants with a low number of MPI
   ranks is enough.

 - This cuts down the number of tests in our testsuite that have a
   concurrency of 10 or more from around 225 to around 190.

   The issue with these tests is the fact that we have to block off
   parallel slots in the ctest run equal to the number of MPI ranks.
   Meaning the more tests we have that have a high number of MPI ranks
   the less optimal the scheduling in ctest.
